sentences.text: This creature possessed a notably shorter tail and a reduced fourth toe compared to its close relative, Archaeopteryx.
It is recognized as an extinct genus of a primitive avialan closely related to Archaeopteryx.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is the Solnhofen Specimen of Archaeopteryx, discovered in the 1960s near Eichstätt, Germany.
Peter Wellnhofer described this fossil in 1988, and it is now housed in the Bürgermeister-Müller-Museum in Solnhofen.
Before its formal recognition, the specimen was originally classified as a Compsognathus by an amateur collector.
Andrzej Elżanowski formally described Wellnhoferia in 2001, establishing the new genus after finding significant differences between the Solnhofen specimen and Archaeopteryx.
Wellnhoferia belongs to the order Archaeopterygiformes, the family Archaeopterygidae, and the parent group Avialae.
The type species of the genus is W. grandis, which was also described by Elżanowski in 2001.
Elżanowski named this new genus after Peter Wellnhofer to honor his earlier work on the fossil.

A 2007 study by Mayr et al. concluded that Wellnhoferia is actually a specimen of Archaeopteryx lithographica, contradicting Elżanowski's original classification. However, Senter and Robins (2003) supported Elżanowski's decision to name Wellnhoferia a new genus.
